seo_title: Miraflora Wagyu Case Study: GWI Audience Insights | SOMIN
description: SOMIN read GWI data on 1,318,330 affluent Colorado cooks for Miraflora Wagyu, which had a high CPA, and found they are deal sensitive, not price sensitive.
eyebrow: Brand case study · Wagyu eCommerce · Colorado, USA
h1: Miraflora Wagyu's buyers are deal sensitive, not price sensitive
lede: Miraflora Wagyu, a premium wagyu eCommerce brand in the USA, faced a high CPA and suspected its price point. SOMIN read GWI survey data on Colorado cooks, tracked 9 beef brands' content in SOMONITOR and compared online prices. Affluent cooks turned out to be deal sensitive: 61.4% use discount codes and 67.0% use loyalty programmes.
meta_line: A SOMIN brand briefing · March to May 2024 · Colorado, USA · Cooks with household income of 85k and above

stats.label: Bought meat online in the last month

challenge.title: Miraflora Wagyu's high CPA and a suspected price problem
challenge.body: Miraflora Wagyu was paying a high cost per acquisition, and its high price point was the suspected culprit: wagyu is about 3x to 16x more expensive than the grass-fed alternative. SOMIN was asked to analyse March to May 2024 competitor content, see how other brands position wagyu when cheaper steaks are available, and look at what influencers were saying.

approach.title: GWI survey data, SOMONITOR tracking and price research
points: Profiled Colorado cooks with the SOMIN x GWI Q2 2024 survey: 2,838,296 people interested in cooking, then the 1,318,330 with household income of 85k and above.
Tracked competitor content in SOMONITOR for 9 brands, including Crowd Cow, Snake River Farms, The Wagyu Shop and Lone Mountain Wagyu, by key message, incentive type and USP.
Mapped Miraflora's communications onto the awareness, consideration, conversion and advocacy funnel.
Compared cost per ounce and cost per portion for ribeye, New York strip and filet mignon across 6 online sellers, plus minimum orders and shipping costs.
Used SoInspire reasoning data to generate emotional moments around holiday meal preparation.

findings_title: What GWI and SOMONITOR showed about Miraflora's buyers

findings.title: Deal sensitive, not price sensitive
findings.body: Among affluent Colorado cooks, 61.0% look for the best deals, 59.3% research before buying and 67.0% use loyalty or reward programmes. Their sensitivity is about getting the best value, not the price itself.

findings.title: Strong on quality, missing from free shipping
findings.body: Most of Miraflora's propositions sell high-quality wagyu beef. Against 8 other brands in 2024, it fell behind on discounting and was non-existent in the free shipping space.

findings.title: Few cooks buy meat online yet
findings.body: 78.7% of affluent Colorado cooks bought meat in the last month, but only 10.1% bought it online. The briefing reads this as an adoption problem.

delivered.title: A 4Ps plan and 6 personas for Miraflora Wagyu
points: 6 SOMONITOR-identified personas, from The Festive Celebrator to The Grill Master, each with an ideal product pairing and a message
Promotional tactics modelled on competitors, such as $25 off the Wagyu Prime Gift Box and free shipping on a first subscription order
Place fixes for freshness concerns, a preference for in-person selection and hesitance to pay for delivery, including free shipping above a set order value
4 emotional moments from SoInspire around holiday meals: anxiety, nostalgia, triumph and frustration
A worked concept for The Festive Celebrator, 'No More Holiday Hosting Stress', with hook, message, CTA and visuals

quote.text: Sensitivity to price is not really about the price but about the perception that they’re getting the best value for their dollar.

outcome.title: Miraflora Wagyu should compete on deals and an easier checkout
outcome.body: The briefing recommends strengthening the promotion strategy rather than competing on price, since direct discounts give customers the perception of getting a steal. It also suggests not forcing a minimum order, absorbing those costs elsewhere in the transaction, and building trust to lift online adoption.

faq.q: What data did SOMIN use for the Miraflora Wagyu case?
faq.a: The SOMIN x GWI Q2 2024 consumer survey (base audience USA, filtered to Colorado and an interest in cooking), SOMONITOR competitor content data, SoInspire reasoning data and online competitor pricing research.

Content tracking covered 7x Beef, Crowd Cow, GoodChop, Grand Western Steaks, Lone Mountain Wagyu, Miraflora Wagyu, Rastelli's, Snake River Farms and The Wagyu Shop. The price research also included The Meatery and Holy Grail.

faq.q: Which personas did SOMIN identify for Miraflora Wagyu?
faq.a: Six SOMONITOR-identified personas: The Festive Celebrator, The Healthy Foodie, The Sustainability Chef, The Culture Explorer, The Family Prepper and The Grill Master, each paired with a product and a message.

faq.q: Where do Colorado cooks find out about brands?
faq.a: Word of mouth leads: the briefing reports that 48.1% of Coloradans find brands through friends and family. Recommendations or comments on social media have the highest index, at 149.7.
